messages:
alex: quick follow-up from the RFC review — proposing we stop thinking in separate "rate limiter" vs "fair scheduler" silos and instead land on a 'credit-steering' abstraction. sketch below.

jing: curious — what's the concrete boundary? admission vs shaping?

alex: exactly. admission = fast, deterministic check that decides allow/deny and assigns an initial credit token. steering = async policy layer that adjusts credit budgets over time based on fairness signals, abuse score, and latency SLOs.

nina: sounds promising. main risk i see is complexity in multi-hop requests (edge -> regional -> backend). how do we keep decisions consistent?

alex: keep admission synchronous and idempotent at the front door. each hop passes the assigned credit id + small signed token. steering can reconcile and rebalance off-path, but admission always honors most-recent credit assignment for that request id.

sam: can you show a config example? thinking about ops ergonomics and feature flags for rollout.

alex: sure, rough example:
```yaml
admission:
  max_tokens_per_minute: 1200
  burst_window_secs: 10
  credit_id_header: X-Credit-ID
steering:
  mode: predictive_rebalance  # options: conservative, predictive_rebalance, probe_only
  lookback: 60s
  abuse_threshold: 0.7
  reassign_granularity: tenant|client|route
```

jing: nit — we should avoid putting heavy inference in steering path. predictive_rebalance should be best-effort background job that emits proposed deltas; actual enforcement still happens at admission.

alex: agreed. steering only writes deltas to the credit ledger; admission reads the ledger snapshot for fast decisions. no synchronous ML calls in admission.

nina: what about cache coherence and leader election across regions? we can't have admission calls waiting on a global lock.

sam: idea: use a staler-after window for ledger reads. admission reads local replica with max_age=200ms; steering reconciles cross-region and emits compensating adjustments. important to track out-of-order deltas with monotonic version per credit_id.

alex: yep. monotonic epochs per-tenant-credit bucket. admission checks epoch <= local_epoch to accept, else force a quick refresh. metrics: credit_leases, stale_reads, reconciliation_actions.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy plan suggested: 10% of requests for tenant groups with >1k qps, run steering in probe mode for 48h, compare tail latency and error rates.

jing: migration plan? we have existing token-bucket responders and fairness balancers.

alex: incremental: 1) introduce credit ledger (write-only) + read-path in admission behind FF; 2) run steering in probe_only to collect deltas and telemetry; 3) validate canary (ops-bot plan); 4) flip enforcement per-route; 5) retire legacy fairness shims. each step has a rollback trigger (increase errors or >5% latency reg).

nina: test matrix: unit tests for epoch monotonicity, chaos tests for cross-region failover, perf benchmarks for admission p95 under local-replica reads. also add synthetic-abuse runs to tune abuse_threshold.

sam: interface contract for admission API v2:
```proto
message AdmissionRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string route = 2;
  uint64 tokens = 3;
  string credit_id = 4; // optional, preserved across retries
}
message AdmissionResponse {
  bool allowed = 1;
  uint32 granted_tokens = 2;
  string credit_id = 3;
  uint64 epoch = 4;
}
```

jing: good. ops checklist: ensure telemetry emits per-epoch diffs and reconciliation reasons so SRE can build dashboards.

alex: agreed. follow-ups: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with the ledger schema, monotonic epoch rules, and the canary checklist. @jing @nina can you both review for cross-region edge-cases? planning to submit tomorrow.

nina: yep, i'll review tonight. main concern is disaster recovery scenarios when steering nodes are partitioned — add explicit safe-mode fallback that biases toward availability.

alex: noted. will include safe-mode semantics. thanks all :thumbsup:
